headline: Russia–Ukraine talks are happening, NATO–Russia clash odds jump, and oil heads back toward $105
summary: A Russia–Ukraine diplomatic meeting by Oct 31 jumped to 98%, but traders also raised the odds of a NATO–Russia military clash this month to 20%. Oil turned back up toward $105. The Fed is now almost certain to hold next week, and a December hike looks a little less certain. About $350k of whale money bet on Republicans keeping the Senate.

takeaways.lead: Russia and Ukraine will meet within days.
takeaways.text: A Russia–Ukraine diplomatic meeting by Oct 31 jumped 79 pts in a day to 97.7%. Peace talks by Nov 30 rose 16 to 79% (up 56 this week). Related: the US importing Russian diesel by Nov 30 rose 11 pts to 78% (up 47 this week), a hint that sanctions could ease.

takeaways.lead: But NATO–Russia clash odds spiked too.
takeaways.text: A NATO–Russia military clash by Oct 31 jumped 12 pts to 20%, and by year-end jumped 10 to 36.5% ($10M market). Large traders bet about $25k that no clash happens this month. Talks and tension are rising at the same time, so expect headline-driven swings.

WTI reaching $105 this month rose 15 pts to 56.5%, and $110 rose 8 to 24%. Oil dropping back to $95 fell 13 pts to 38% (down 51 this week). The Middle East ceasefires steadied (US–Iran through Oct 31: 76.5%, up 3), but Iran closing its airspace by Oct 31 rose 5 pts to 11.5%.

takeaways.lead: The Fed is almost certain to hold, and December is less certain.
takeaways.text: No change at the Oct 29 meeting rose 5 pts to 93.5%, with about $79k of large bets on it. A December hike fell 5 pts to 73.5%, and a January hike fell 8 to 29.5%. Canada still looks set to hike (81%).

takeaways.lead: Big money is betting Republicans keep the Senate.
takeaways.text: One trader put $151k against Democrats taking the Senate, $111k went against a Democratic sweep, and $75k more went on a Republican sweep at 8¢. That's about $350k on the Republican side. The odds barely moved: Democrats take the Senate 67.5%, and Democrats take the House 92.5% (with $132k of large bets on that).

takeaways.lead: Anthropic's next model looks delayed (thin signal).
takeaways.text: Fable 5.2 releasing by Oct 31 fell 33 pts to 25% (down 62 this week; $308k traded on that date). Anthropic's valuation hitting $1.75T by year-end still rose 9 to 79.5%. Yesterday's Celonis IPO jump fully reversed (down 37 to 7.4%), a reminder that thin markets whipsaw.

sections.title: What's new today
bullets: France accusing a foreign country of provoking its unrest by Nov 30 rose 8 pts to 15.5% (new, thin $22k market).
Russia's central bank decided not to cut rates (that market is at 100%).
Russia capturing the Ukrainian town of Vodianske by year-end rose 12 pts to 56% (thin market), so fighting continues even as talks start.

sections.title: Trading signals
bullets: Oil: WTI $105 this month 56.5% (up 15), $110 24%. Upside risk is back.
Rates: Fed hold 93.5%, Fed December hike 73.5% (down 5). Bond yields: the 10-year reaching 5.7% this year fell 9 pts to 5.3%.
AI: Anthropic IPO by Dec 15 is 84% (up 16 this week). OpenAI's IPO closing above $1.2T rose 12 pts to 62%. Google is the clear favorite for the best AI model at the end of October (86%).
Apple as the largest company at the end of October rose 8 pts to 21%.

sections.title: Wars & geopolitics
bullets: NATO–Russia clash by year-end: 36.5% (up 10). This is the highest-stakes number on the page right now.
Israel–Iran ceasefire through Oct 31: 85.5% (up 4); through Nov 15: 58.5% (down 11 this week).
Large traders sold $28k of 'Iranian regime survives 2026', a small bet on regime change (now 5.5%).

sections.title: Elections that move markets
bullets: Brazil (Sunday, Oct 25): Bolsonaro 77%, Lula 23.5% (up 2). The final days are tightening slightly.
Israel (Oct 27): Eizenkot 49.2%, Netanyahu 28.5% (up 2), Bennett 15.5%. A $30k bet went on Netanyahu.
US midterms (Nov 3): Democrats take the Senate 67.5%, the House 92.5%, and both 66.5%.

sections.title: Everyday life
bullets: Gas: oil is turning back up toward $105, so pump prices likely stay high into November.
US borrowing: no change from the Fed next week (93.5%), and December hike odds are slipping (73.5%), which is slightly good news for loans.
Canadian borrowers: a rate hike next Wednesday is 81% likely.
